title: Evaluation of Argogen for Treatment of Pressure Ulcers in Clinical Follow-Up Study
author: Dionisio Franco Barattini

steps.title: Screen Patients for Eligibility
steps.instruction: Screen patients to ensure they have minor burn wounds (superficial or superficial/deep partial-thickness) or chronic pressure ulcers stage 2 or 3 (NPUAP Classification).

substeps.instruction: Verify absence of severe organ disease (heart, brain, liver, kidney, lung).
Confirm no untreated diabetes mellitus or diabetic foot syndrome.
Ensure Peripheral Artery Disease ABI is ≥ 0.9.
Verify Platelets ≥ 150,000 g/l and Haemoglobin ≥ 95 g/l (collected within last 3 months).
Confirm absence of concomitant infection at other sites, osteomyelitis, erysipelas, or phlegmon.
Ensure no complicated deep tissue infection requiring systemic antimicrobial therapy.
Confirm no active viral hepatitis (A/B/C), HIV, or syphilis.
Verify no neoplastic growth in the ulcer.
Confirm no impairment of the cochlea or vestibularis system or neuromuscular diseases (e.g., myasthenia gravis, Parkinson's).
Ensure no aminoglycoside or other antibiotic treatments for chronic venous ulcers within 4 weeks before inclusion.
Confirm no use of proteolytic enzymes (bromelain, chymotrypsin, ficin, papain, serrapeptase, trypsin) during the study.
Exclude pregnant or lactating women and those planning pregnancy or unwilling to use contraception.
Confirm no known allergy to silver or Argogen components.
Ensure no participation in other interventional clinical studies or investigational agents in the previous 30 days.

steps.title: Establish Baseline (Day 0)
steps.instruction: Perform the screening/baseline visit and record initial wound metrics.

substeps.instruction: For pressure ulcers: Record PUSH ver. 3.0 score (length x width, exudate amount, and tissue type).
For burn wounds: Record VSS score (vascularity, height/thickness, pliability, and pigmentation).
Administer the first dose of Argogen.

steps.title: Apply Argogen Treatment
steps.instruction: Apply Argogen (silver zeolite powder, 2.5% ionic silver) to all affected body areas, focusing on the target wound for evaluation.

substeps.instruction: Apply the spray powder twice a day from day 0 to week 2.
If requested by Investigators, continue administration for an additional 2 weeks until day 28.
Do not exceed 4 weeks of total treatment.

steps.title: Conduct Interim and Final Evaluations
steps.instruction: Perform follow-up visits to monitor healing and safety at specified intervals.

substeps.instruction: Week 1 (± 1 day): Perform interim visit.
Week 2 (± 1 day): Perform interim visit; evaluate PUSH score (pressure ulcers) or VSS score (burns) and record Pain assessment via 100 mm Visual Analogue Scale (VAS).
Week 4 (± 2 days): Perform final visit; evaluate PUSH score (pressure ulcers) or VSS score (burns).
Week 4: Administer Treatment satisfaction questionnaire and Pain assessment (VAS).
Week 4: Perform Investigator Global Assessment of Performance (IGAP) using photos from each visit.
Week 4: Perform Investigator Global Assessment of Safety (IGAS) and Patient Global Assessment of Safety (PGAS).

steps.title: Monitor Safety Endpoints
steps.instruction: Track and report safety data throughout the 28-day study duration.

substeps.instruction: Assess and report incidence of AEs, SAEs, ADE, SADE, ASADE, and USADE.

description: In- or outpatients of both sexes, of all ethnic backgrounds, aged between 18 and 75 years (inclusive). Patients presenting superficial / first degree and superficial / deep partial-thickness / second- degree burn wound in less than 10% of total body surface area, for which the burning eventoccurred within 48 hours and that can be treatedwithin 24 hours after enrolment in the study (at baseline) or Patients presenting chronic pressure ulcers stage 2 or 3 (according to the NPUAPClassification) that did not heal within 3 weeks despite proper wound care, with areas (or scattered areas) of necrosis (nonviable soft tissue/slough) more than 40%, and with a target wound which is between 4 cm squared to 20 cm squared in area at the baseline assessment. Patients, who are, in the opinion of the Investigator, able to understand this study, cooperate with the study procedures and are willing to return to the centre (if outpatients) for all the required visits. Patients who have given their written informed consent in accordance with provisions of pertinent excerpt from the Declaration of Helsinki and the Romanian laws. The principle of intention-to-treat (ITT),as far as practically possible,will be the main strategy of theanalysis adopted for the primary endpoint and all the secondary endpoints. These analyses will be conducted on all participants. No imputations will be made on missing data. The statistical plan details the following 3 analysis sets ITT, Per-Protocol, Safety populations. The protocol outlines that a two-sided p-value of 0.05 or less will be used to declare statistical significance for all analyses. Similarly, all confidence intervals will be calculated at the 95% level. No adjustment for multiplicity will be made to adjust type 1 error rate for secondary endpoints.
